nodes.title: Almost Halving a Three-Branched Tree
nodes.milestone: Deliver a mathematical document and a standard-library command-line checker, obtained from the public repository with one documented command and a real recorded run. For positive integers a,b,c, let T have one centre and three paths of a,b,c further vertices. Prove disjoint equal-size subsets with identical multisets of all pairwise distances, each of size at least floor((1+a+b+c)/2)-1, or give an infinite structural obstruction family with a rigorous upper bound refuting that target. First independently reconstruct the published cases, fixing endpoints explicitly, and refresh priority. A signed distance-shell formulation may guide the work; it is not an algorithmic or mathematical result already delivered. No gallery simulation or finite census substitutes for the proof. Acceptance: A non-author reconstructs the argument for every length and parity class and writes an independent distance counter for fresh unequal triples. They verify disjointness, size and multiplicities, and ensure a deliberately altered pair is rejected. For a negative family they audit the upper bound over every permitted pair, not just failed search branches. Drop for a missed case, an unsupported endpoint repair, prior resolution, only finite experiments, or a result about isometry instead of equal distance multisets. Priority must be stated provisionally until the unread sources are resolved.
nodes.plain: Can almost all dots on three paths meeting at one junction be split into two equal groups with exactly the same distance counts? A proof would answer a concrete question about branching networks.
